title: Choose the DevPay website's visual world
question: The roll assigned Adinkra Stamped Cloth, in the app's own colours. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Adinkra Stamped Cloth
options.lineage: Ntonso adinkra printing: comb-ruled grids, carved calabash stamps, badie ink
options.thesis: Every milestone is a square on the cloth, stamped as the money moves.
options.viewport: A ruled cloth band carries three milestone squares stamped Funded, Delivered, Released beside 'Money first. Then the work.' and a Download APK button.
options.risk: Stamps turn into decoration if each one isn't tied to a real escrow state.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: funded, delivered and released are stamp impressions, never coloured badges.
One axis: the page descends a single ruled length of cloth, section by section.
Every part of the escrow demo carries its plain printed label.
The visitor's tap stamps the next square, and the cloth keeps it.
Squares the money hasn't reached stay pale and unstamped.

options.label: Cedi Note Security Print
options.lineage: Bank of Ghana cedi notes: guilloche, intaglio, serial numbers
options.thesis: The site printed like a banknote: guilloche rosettes, serials and the logo as a watermark.
options.viewport: A note-proportioned panel with a guilloche rosette, the headline set like a denomination, and the APK button as the serial strip.
options.risk: Banknote styling is the obvious money metaphor most fintech sites reach for.

options.label: Developer Console
options.thesis: DevPay as a console: the escrow ledger in panels split by hairline seams.
options.viewport: Tiled panels: a live escrow ledger, a milestone timeline and the install command beside the headline.
options.case: Developers recognise it at once; clients and non-developer freelancers don't.
options.risk: Near-black with one accent is the look AI sites default to.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Sections strung along a perforated rail like film frames.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crossing an orange field with frames for each step.
options.risk: Film editing means nothing to a freelancer waiting on MoMo.
options.case: Loses both axes: foreign to the audience and it hides the offer.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: The page as an axial garden walk.
options.viewport: An axial vista with parterres either side.
options.risk: Royal spectacle contradicts a calm money product.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to Ghana or to escrow.
options.kept: One axis the whole page descends.

options.label: Busytown Cutaway
options.thesis: Accra as a labelled cutaway town where escrow happens.
options.viewport: A cutaway street with labelled workers.
options.risk: Childlike tone undercuts trust with money.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful where visitors need reassurance.
options.kept: Every object carries its plain label.

options.label: Minihompy Room
options.thesis: Your DevPay profile as a room you furnish.
options.viewport: An isometric room with counters around it.
options.risk: Social decoration is unrelated to getting paid.
options.kept: Visitor actions leave a lasting change.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: A dark sea that lights up where you move.
options.risk: Glow effects are the neon-on-black default and slow on budget phones.

canonCard.label: The fintech landing standard
canonCard.thesis: What fintech apps ship: headline, phone mock-up, feature grid, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and Download button left, app screenshot in a phone frame right, features below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other fintech site by design.
